audit.why: 47.19% over 693 games. The chart gives Camille levels 1-3 and level 6 and calls the item stages Skill, while the prose says Vayne takes the game back at two items. The early stages are right — a level-1 Vayne with no Silver Bolts stacks and no Condemn is not a threat — and the honest late-game read is already written.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 is written entirely as Camille's spike — 'your single best kill button all game' — and Final Hour is never mentioned anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: Vayne also reaches 6. Final Hour is a 100s ultimate at rank 1 that gives her bonus attack damage and, critically, invisibility during Tumble — the text even refers to her ability to 'invis away' without ever saying where it comes from. A player told level 6 is a one-sided spike will R into a Vayne who has just ulted and lose the trade she was promised.
audit.corrected: Final Hour named and its 100s cooldown given, with the Tumble-stealth tied to it; level 6 still Camille's stage but with the condition stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Condemn is written in lower case as a generic noun ('condemn', 'her condemn (E)') and Tumble as 'Q tumble'. wants.foe[1] says 'Stack the third Silver Bolt' — the ability is Silver Bolts. Camille's R appears without its article.
audit.why: The cooldown arithmetic behind this lane is never given and it is decisive: Condemn is 20s at rank 1, falling to 12s at rank 5, against Hookshot's 16s. At rank 1 her escape is on a LONGER cooldown than Camille's engage, which is exactly why levels 2-5 are Camille's window and why that window narrows as Vayne ranks E. Tumble at 6s down to 2s is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up before it is the tell that a burst is coming rather than the ability cast itself. Condemn also stuns if it pins a target to terrain — and Camille's own engage requires her to be next to terrain, which is the trap the mid section gestures at without explaining.
audit.corrected: Condemn, Tumble, Silver Bolts and Final Hour all named properly; Condemn's 20s-to-12s range and Tumble's auto-reset tell written in; the wall-stun risk stated as the reason her engage position is dangerous.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Force all-ins on her condemn cooldown' and 'bait her condemn, then E in on the cooldown' name the cooldown three times without ever giving it.
audit.why: 20s at rank 1 against Hookshot's 16s is the single most encouraging number in this matchup and it degrades to 12s against 12s by rank 5. Stating it tells the player both why to fight early and why the window closes.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to wants.you[2] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Position so a missed knock-back doesn't pin you to a wall' explains the consequence but not the mechanic.
audit.why: Condemn stuns when it knocks a champion into terrain. Camille is the champion most often standing beside terrain, because Hookshot needs a wall to anchor to. The two facts together mean her best engage position is also her worst Condemn position, and that trade-off should be stated rather than hinted.

edits.before: Level 1 is hers — you have one ability and no all-in while she kites you with autos and Q tumble, and you eat free percent-HP true poke from her third Silver Bolt if you walk up. Hold your ground, last-hit, and wait. At Level 2 your Precision Protocol re-cast (the second hit adds true damage and a brief move-speed pop) comes online and the lane flips: E in, Q twice, and burn her health bar before condemn and a stacked Silver Bolt are real threats. Your passive shield absorbs her first auto, so trade through it and bait the condemn — once her E is down you can dive freely.
edits.after: Level 1 is hers — you have one ability and no all-in while she kites you with autos and Tumble, and the third Silver Bolts hit adds true damage if you walk up. Hold your ground, last-hit, and wait. At Level 2 your Precision Protocol re-cast (the second hit adds true damage and a brief move-speed pop) comes online and the lane flips: E in, Q twice, and burn her health bar before Condemn and stacked Silver Bolts are real threats. Adaptive Defenses appears once your own attack lands, so open the trade rather than waiting on it, and bait Condemn — 20s at rank 1, longer than your Hookshot.

edits.before: Levels 3-5 are your bully window — you out-trade a pre-item Vayne hard because her short trades lose to your Q true damage and Tactical Sweep's outer-edge max-HP slash and self-heal. Force every all-in here. At 6, Hextech Ultimatum answers everything she does: lock her in the arena and she can't tumble out, can't condemn you to safety, and can't kite — it's an isolated 1v1 you win. The danger is her condemn when you dive: position so a missed knock-back doesn't pin you to a wall, and don't blow R until she has wasted tumble.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 are your bully window — a pre-item Vayne loses short trades to your Q true damage and Tactical Sweep's outer edge and self-heal. Force every all-in inside Condemn's 20s. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum answers Tumble and Condemn both, but open it while Final Hour is spent. The real danger is where you stand: Condemn stuns when it pins you to terrain, and Hookshot needs terrain — so the wall you grappled from is the wall she wants behind you. Angle off it before you commit.

notes: Final Hour was absent from the entire matchup even though the text twice describes Vayne 'invis'-ing away — that stealth is Final Hour-gated, on a 100s cooldown, and it turns the level-6 entry from a one-sided spike into a conditional one. UNVERIFIED: the existing text calls Silver Bolts' third hit 'percent-HP true damage' in three places. Riot's data flags the ability as true damage but carries no percentHealth flag, and I could not confirm the max-health component from the kits, so I removed the percent-HP wording only where I was already rewriting the line and left the claim itself alone rather than asserting either way. _missing-interactions.json also generates a 'Condemn cancels your R channel' line for this matchup; The Hextech Ultimatum is a dash in Riot's own text, not a channel, so I did not write it.
